# Kontora

> Agent orchestration daemon with a kanban board. Runs AI coding agents through multi-stage pipelines with git worktree isolation.

- Repository: https://github.com/worksonmyai/kontora

You are helping a user install and set up Kontora. Follow these steps in order.

## Overview

Kontora watches a directory of ticket files (markdown with YAML frontmatter), picks up tickets with `status: todo`, creates a git worktree per ticket, runs AI agents in tmux sessions, and tracks progress through configurable pipeline stages (e.g. implement → review → fix → commit). It has a web dashboard, a terminal TUI, and a CLI.

## Prerequisites

- macOS or Linux
- [git](https://git-scm.com/) — for worktree management
- [tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux) — agents run in detached tmux sessions
- At least one AI coding agent: [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) (`claude`), [Pi](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/packages/pi) (`pi`), [OpenCode](https://github.com/opencode-ai/opencode) (`opencode`), or any CLI that accepts a prompt

Verify prerequisites:

```bash
git --version && tmux -V
```

## Step 1: Install

Homebrew:

```bash
brew tap worksonmyai/kontora https://github.com/worksonmyai/kontora
brew install kontora
```

From source (Go 1.26+):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/worksonmyai/kontora.git && cd kontora && make install
```

Verify: `kontora version`

## Step 2: Configure

Run this and follow what it prints:

```bash
kontora setup --agent
```

The installed binary prints a setup brief for you: the config path and its current state, the questions to ask the user, the validation rules, and how to write the file without losing the user's settings. The brief ships inside the binary, so it matches the schema this version accepts. Follow it instead of a schema you remember, and instead of the configuration reference on the web.

`kontora setup --agent` only prints. It never writes the config.

If the user would rather do it themselves, tell them to run `kontora setup` for the interactive wizard. When they are done, read `~/.config/kontora/config.yaml` and offer to review it.

## Step 3: Verify and start

```bash
kontora doctor   # checks config, tools, agent binaries, port availability
```

Then tell the user to run `kontora start` in a separate terminal — it starts the daemon and web dashboard and runs in the foreground.

## Step 4: Usage

Create a ticket:

```bash
cd ~/projects/myrepo
kontora new "Add a health check endpoint"
```

With explicit path and pipeline:

```bash
kontora new --path ~/projects/myrepo --pipeline implement-review-commit "Add a health check endpoint"
```

Without `--pipeline`, the ticket takes the pipeline of the project that owns the repository, then the top-level `default_pipeline`. When neither names one, the ticket runs a single agent on its description rather than a pipeline. `--pipeline none` asks for that on purpose.

Web dashboard: open http://127.0.0.1:8080 (kanban board with live agent terminal view).

TUI: `kontora` or `kontora ls`.

Monitor: `kontora attach` (tmux session), `kontora logs <id>`.

Manage: `kontora pause <id>`, `kontora retry <id>`, `kontora done <id>`, `kontora cancel <id>`, `kontora note <id> "message"`.

## Remote mode

The CLI can drive a daemon on another machine over its HTTP/SSE/WebSocket API. Intended for a trusted network (e.g. a Tailscale tailnet).

Daemon host config — bind to the tailnet IP and set a shared token:

```yaml
web:
  host: 100.x.y.z   # tailnet IP, not 127.0.0.1
  port: 8080
  token: <a-long-random-secret>
```

When `web.token` is set, the daemon requires it on `/api/*` and `/ws/*`. `GET /health` and the static UI stay public. The browser bootstraps auth by opening `http://<host>:8080/?token=<secret>`, which sets a `kontora_token` cookie.

Client — set `KONTORA_URL` and `KONTORA_TOKEN` (or `--url`/`--token`); no local config file is needed:

```bash
export KONTORA_URL=http://100.x.y.z:8080
export KONTORA_TOKEN=<the-same-secret>
kontora ls
kontora run <id>
kontora logs <id>
kontora attach <id>   # live terminal over WebSocket
```

Remote mode supports `ls`, `view`, `new`, `init`, `update`, `delete`, `run`, `pause`, `retry`, `cancel`, `done`, `skip`, `set-stage`, `note`, `summary`, `logs`, `config`, `attach`. Local-only verbs (`edit`, `archive`, `fmt`, `doctor`, `start`, `setup`, `completion`) are rejected. Run setup on the daemon host. Paths for `kontora new --path` are on the daemon host, not the caller.

Security: the token is the only access control, and agents run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. A tailnet encrypts the transport, so plain HTTP is fine there. On any untrusted network, terminate TLS in front of the daemon — the bearer token is otherwise sent in clear.

Ticket format and lifecycle: [docs/tickets.md](https://github.com/worksonmyai/kontora/blob/main/docs/tickets.md)
